purpose: Explicit, machine-readable record of which Eve sessions count toward the pre-registered 8-session bar, and why -- so this can never later look like moving the goalposts. See docs/eve_engine_v1_session0_closing_report.md for the full narrative.

pre_registration.eve_must_clear: 5% OOS survival, FDR-corrected PER SESSION (each of the 8 pre-registered sessions independently clears its own 5%-FDR-corrected bar -- this is NOT one pooled correction spanning all 8 sessions' hypotheses together)
pre_registration.eve_must_clear_original_wording: 5% OOS survival, FDR-corrected, across the full cross-asset family

eve_must_clear_reframe_provenance.reason: CC-1 Factory Loop directive item 3: truth-in-labeling only, no verdict/threshold changed. The original phrase above is genuinely ambiguous between 'each session's own family, corrected independently' (what nero_core.eve.scoring.apply_fdr_correction has always actually done -- confirmed directly at its call site in nero_core/eve/pipeline.py, which runs it once per session against that session's own hypothesis_records only) and 'one family spanning all 8 sessions' (the more natural reading of the phrase itself). Rather than silently overwrite the original claim, it is preserved verbatim above (eve_must_clear_original_wording) and eve_must_clear itself is rewritten to state plainly what the code actually does. apply_fdr_correction's mechanism and per-session scope are UNCHANGED by this reframe -- see docs/investigations/factory_loop_specification.md's own B4 for the honest assessment that per-session correction, while defensible for a small fixed 8-session pre-registered campaign, would need an explicit rolling-family or reframed-claim decision before any open-ended continuous loop launches (a separate, not-yet-made decision, out of scope for this reframe).

freshness_gate_reversal_provenance.reason: CC-1 correction directive: item 7's search-freshness disqualification (nero_core.eve.scoring.check_freshness_disqualification, Variant C, 30-day window) was made BINDING in commit 61d78a8 -- gating nero_core.research_agent.trial.admit_to_trial's admission (item 4e) and excluded from apply_fdr_correction's family (item 7c). It was reverted to informational-only the same day. Reason: the check is necessarily SESSION-SCOPED, not per-hypothesis -- nero_core.eve.scoring's own session log has no structural way to associate a specific web_search_tool_result with the specific propose_hypothesis call it may have informed (see check_freshness_disqualification's own PER-HYPOTHESIS ATTRIBUTION LIMITATION docstring section). One qualifying search result therefore disqualifies every hypothesis in the session that produced it, not just the ones it plausibly informed. Combined with item 7c's FDR-family exclusion, this made the pre-registered 'X% OOS survival, FDR-corrected per session' criterion unsatisfiable BY CONSTRUCTION whenever a session both performs a live web search (which every real Eve session does) and that search happens to surface anything published in the preceding 30 days -- not a finding ABOUT Eve's real survival rate, but an artifact of the gate's own necessarily-coarse scope. Confirmed directly against the real Eve Session 1 file (eve-20260804T020749Z-4cf6e4c9.json, re-scored 2026-08-05): 100% of that session's 5 backtested hypotheses would have been disqualified, not the ~33% originally estimated. The 30-day window itself was not the variable -- narrowing or widening it does not fix the underlying scope problem, since one search per session is enough regardless of the exact threshold. Reverted rather than retuned. All of item 7's INFORMATIONAL machinery (check_freshness_disqualification, apply_freshness_disqualification, the freshness_disqualified/freshness_disqualification_reason audit fields, and the freshness_disqualified_entire_session fail-loud session flag) remains live and unchanged -- only the two BINDING consequences (Trial admission gating, FDR-family exclusion) were removed. See nero_core.research_agent.trial.admit_to_trial's own docstring and nero_core.eve.scoring.apply_fdr_correction's own docstring for the code-level record of the same reversal.
freshness_gate_reversal_provenance.any_countable_session_ran_while_binding_: Confirmed by direct inspection of every file under docs/site_data/eve_sessions/ on 2026-08-05 (3 real session files: eve-20260803T095520Z-394385c7.json, eve-20260803T142519Z-718833c9.json, eve-20260804T020749Z-4cf6e4c9.json -- all three predate commit 61d78a8's own timestamp, and none carries a freshness_disqualified_entire_session or freshness_disqualification_flags field at all, confirming the informational item 7 machinery has never even been RUN against any of them, let alone the binding gate). Also confirmed: docs/site_data/eve_hypotheses.json (16 records) contains zero records with freshness_disqualified=true or an excluded_from_fdr_family_reason mentioning freshness_disqualified, and docs/site_data/forward_trial.json does not exist on disk at all -- nothing has ever been admitted to or rejected from Trial under any rule, binding or otherwise. This is a confirmed fact derived from data, not an assumption.
freshness_gate_reversal_provenance.homogeneity_confirmation: Because no countable session ran between commit 61d78a8 (binding gate enabled) and this same-day revert, Session 1 (the only countable session to date) and Sessions 2-8 (not yet run) will all run under the IDENTICAL rule set: informational-only freshness disqualification, DSL-validity-only Trial admission, self-derivative-only FDR-family exclusion. The pre-registered 8-session experiment remains homogeneous -- no countable session's own results were produced under a since-reverted rule that a later session would not also have been subject to.

per_hypothesis_citation_freshness_proven.reason: CC-1 directive (per-hypothesis freshness attribution via explicit source citation): rather than constrain Eve's search-then-propose research process to make causal ordering meaningful (confirmed, per the 3697e75 correction, to still yield 100% disqualification -- Eve front-loads all searching before proposing), Eve now explicitly declares which of a session's own real search results support each hypothesis, via an optional `supporting_source_urls` field on propose_hypothesis (nero_core.eve.tools_defs, nero_core.eve.hypothesis_shapes). nero_core.eve.scoring.check_per_hypothesis_freshness attributes freshness risk ONLY to a hypothesis's own validated citations -- a sibling to check_freshness_disqualification (session-wide, unchanged), never a replacement. Cited URLs are validated against the session's own real web_search_tool_result data; an unvalidated URL is a hard error, surfaced via a stderr WARNING and an explicit supporting_source_urls_invalid field, never a silent pass.
per_hypothesis_citation_freshness_proven.strictly_informational: Identical posture to the freshness_gate_reversal_provenance entry above: admit_to_trial and apply_fdr_correction have no code path that reads citation_status or per_hypothesis_freshness at all (see NeverBindingRegressionTest in tests/test_eve_citation_freshness.py). No bar constant (30/yr frequency, 70/30 split, MIN_SAMPLE_SIZE=20, FDR alpha=0.05, bootstrap CI, random-baseline comparison) was changed.
per_hypothesis_citation_freshness_proven.pre_citation_backfill: All 16 records in docs/site_data/eve_hypotheses.json (spanning Session 0, Session 0-B, and Session 1 -- every committed session, not just Session 1) predate this mechanism and were marked citation_status='unscoreable_pre_citation' by the one-time tools/backfill_eve_pre_citation_status.py migration, so they can never be misread as 'checked, found clean.' No retroactive citation was fabricated for any of them.
per_hypothesis_citation_freshness_proven.incentive_analysis: The proposer (Eve) and the cited evidence (her own search log) are the same party. If freshness disqualification ever became binding, Eve would have a direct incentive to omit a recent source from her citation list -- and unlike fabrication, omission cannot be caught by validating citations against the search log, since an omitted URL simply never appears as a claim to validate. This is currently UNLEARNABLE by Eve: scoring runs as a separate pass after session.run_session returns (nero_core.eve.pipeline.run_pipeline), and no freshness or citation outcome is fed back into nero_core.eve.context (Adam-history/graveyard, whitelisted fields only, no verdict/freshness field), hypothesis_gen's prompt building (nero_core.research_agent never imports nero_core.eve), or any other session-context path -- confirmed directly from code, not assumed. This design is sound ONLY while the flag stays informational; the incentive question must be explicitly reopened before any future decision routes freshness outcomes back into agent context or makes the flag binding.

inheritance_regime_provenance.reason: CC-1 directive: 'Making the Loop Evolutionary' shipped a real change to what Eve inherits between sessions -- REFINEMENT tagging (B1) moves a declared, validated refinement of a prior hypothesis back INTO the FDR family instead of excluding it as SELF_DERIVATIVE, and B2 supplies near-miss hypotheses (real p_value_is FDR-significant, p_value_oos not) as session context, an inheritance channel that read an empty set before this directive. Session 1 (eve-20260804T020749Z-4cf6e4c9) ran before any of this existed. Sessions 2-8 (not yet run) will run under the changed regime. This mirrors the freshness_gate_reversal_provenance entry's own homogeneity concern (see above) but is NOT the same shape: that reversal made Session 1 and Sessions 2-8 IDENTICAL again (same-day revert, no countable session ran under the binding gate). This change does NOT revert -- it is a permanent regime split. Session 1 is pre_inheritance; Sessions 2-8 are post_inheritance. The 8-session result, once complete, spans two regimes and cannot cleanly falsify either alone -- see this same directive's own closing report (docs/investigations/factory_loop_implementation_report.md) for the honest reading of what the combined result can and cannot support.
inheritance_regime_provenance.kill_criterion_unchanged: The pre-registered kill criterion itself (5% OOS survival, FDR-corrected PER SESSION -- see eve_must_clear above) is completely unchanged by this directive. Only what Eve is shown/permitted to declare between sessions changed, never what counts as proof of survival.

counting_rule: A session counts toward the pre-registered 8 only once it produces at least one hypothesis that was actually eligible to be scored against real data (i.e. the session ran to completion and the DSL vocabulary / pre-submit validator fix, both landed 2026-08-03, were in place). A session that crashed before completion, or whose every hypothesis was UNTESTABLE_BY_DSL purely because of a since-fixed spec defect (the DSL vocabulary was withheld from Eve, not just strategy examples), produces no data point toward the 5% OOS bar -- an unscoreable hypothesis is not a survival rate of zero, it is an unknown. The 5%/8-session bar itself is UNCHANGED; only what qualifies as a countable session is defined here, before any survival data exists under the fixed system.

The original spec deliberately withheld Adam's schema so Eve would think freely rather than fill in a form -- correct intent, wrong scope: withholding the VOCABULARY is different from withholding the CONSTRAINTS. Fixed same-day: nero_core.eve.session now supplies the exact DSL vocabulary (ALLOWED_FIELDS, ALLOWED_OPS, exact key names, one worked example) in the system prompt, plus a pre-submit validator that returns the parser's own error and offers up to 2 correction retries before finalizing a hypothesis as UNTESTABLE_BY_DSL.
